areas.name: 9 · Estate Planning
areas.note: Will/POA and binding nomination wording is verbatim. Testamentary trust is a draft.

scenarios.name: Prepare / review your Will
scenarios.strat: We recommend that you approach a solicitor to ensure that you have a valid and updated Will in place.
scenarios.outcome: A current Will ensures your assets are distributed according to your wishes.
why: Control — a Will names the beneficiaries who receive your assets and on what terms, and appoints an executor to manage the distribution.
Intestacy — without a valid Will, your assets would be distributed by a prescribed government formula and possibly not in accordance with your wishes.
Relevance — a Will should be updated at least every three years and after any major change in circumstances.
risks: If you fail to update your Will following marriage or divorce it may be rendered invalid, possibly resulting in parts of your estate not being distributed according to your wishes.
alts: (estate documents are essential — no alternative presented)

scenarios.name: Prepare / review Power of Attorney
scenarios.strat: We recommend that you approach a solicitor to ensure that you have a valid and updated Power of Attorney in place.
scenarios.outcome: A Power of Attorney ensures someone you trust can manage your affairs if you are unable to.
why: A Power of Attorney allows a trusted person to make financial/legal decisions on your behalf if you are unable to do so.
risks: A Power of Attorney is a significant document granting authority to act on your behalf — ensure you appoint someone you trust.
alts: (estate documents are essential — no alternative presented)

scenarios.name: Non-lapsing binding death benefit nomination (super)
scenarios.strat: We recommend you choose a non-lapsing binding death nomination within your superannuation funds.
scenarios.outcome: A binding nomination ensures your super death benefit is paid according to your wishes.
why: A non-lapsing binding nomination binds the trustee to pay your super death benefit according to your wishes and remains in force until amended or revoked (subject to the fund's Trust Deed).
Death benefit payment option — you can nominate dependants under the non-lapsing binding election, or you can select an automatic reversionary pension under the pension plan.
risks: When you die, the proceeds from your superannuation fund may be subject to tax if paid as a lump sum to non-dependants. (delete if the fund cannot offer this nomination)

scenarios.name: Testamentary trust
scenarios.strat: We recommend that you contact a solicitor to ensure that you have a valid and updated testamentary trust in place.
scenarios.outcome: A testamentary trust can provide tax‑effective and protected distribution of your estate.
why: Tax Benefits — a testamentary trust allows trustees to distribute and split the income of the trust with tax planning in mind.
Asset Protection — the trust holds the title to the trust's assets (rather than the beneficiaries directly), allowing the trust to protect assets from any litigation, bankruptcy or legal action.

Flexibility — a testamentary trust can provide great flexibility to suit individual circumstances. For example, it is possible to restrict access to assets or distributions to a particular beneficiary.
risks: Your solicitor may charge a fee to review / update your Wills and/or Powers of Attorney.
Estate planning laws vary between Australian states and territories as well as between countries. For this reason, it is important to ensure that your Will is valid for the state in which you live.
A Will does not expire and it is therefore important to have it reviewed and updated if or when your situation changes.
Should you fail to update your Will following marriage or divorce it will render it invalid, possibly resulting in parts of your estate not being distributed according to your wishes.
alts: Distribute the estate directly via the Will — discounted where the tax and asset-protection benefits of a testamentary trust are valuable to your beneficiaries.

scenarios.name: Apply for the Centrelink Age Pension (retirement trigger)
scenarios.gate: Client(s) reaching/at Age Pension age and retiring or reducing work
scenarios.strat: We recommend that next financial year, when you retire or reduce your work, you apply for the Centrelink Age Pension.
scenarios.outcome: You access government income support to supplement your pension drawdowns once retired.
why: On full retirement you may be entitled to a meaningful fortnightly payment as a homeowner, supplementing your account-based pension income and reducing the drawdown pressure on your super.

Eligibility for the Age Pension may also entitle you to additional Commonwealth concessions, including the Pensioner Concession Card — which may provide access to subsidised pharmaceutical costs under the PBS and other state-based concessions. Eligibility is determined by Services Australia and subject to ongoing assessment.
risks: Entitlement depends on the assets and income tests at the time; rates and thresholds are subject to change and indexation.
alts: Rely solely on pension drawdowns — discounted as it forgoes available government support.

scenarios.name: Use the My Wealth Portal

scenarios.outcome: Consolidating your finances in one place streamlines administration and keeps you on track.
why: The My Wealth Portal will allow you to consolidate your financial world into one place, streamlining administration.
The My Wealth Portal includes an automated budgeting system which provides clarity and allows you to take control of your cashflow.
Allows you to build personalised cash flow targets and goals which keep you accountable over time.

scenarios.outcome: Using the recommended platform provides access to the recommended investment menu with competitive administration costs.

The CARE Essentials investment option is only available in the Hub24 platform.
Provides consolidated reporting and the ability for your adviser to manage your portfolio efficiently.

scenarios.outcome: Holding investments in a bucket company caps the tax on retained earnings at the corporate rate and provides a flexible structure for reinvestment.
why: Caps tax on retained investment earnings at the corporate tax rate (25%/30%) rather than higher personal marginal rates.
Provides a flexible, long-term vehicle for accumulating and reinvesting trust distributions.
risks: Franking credits, Division 7A and distribution rules apply; obtain advice from your accountant. The company structure has ongoing administration and compliance costs.

why: Allows flexible distribution of income/capital to beneficiaries to manage the family's overall tax position.
Provides a degree of asset protection.
risks: Trust income must generally be distributed each year; undistributed income is taxed at the top marginal rate. Obtain advice from your accountant on distributions and Division 7A where a company is a beneficiary.

scenarios.outcome: You hold a dedicated Reserves buffer that is continually topped up from portfolio income, so income and rebalancing can be funded without selling growth assets at the wrong time during a market downturn.
why: A key benefit of the CARE approach is the separation of your investments into Core, Active, Reserves and Enhanced components, allowing the Reserves component to be continually topped up with income from the others.

This matters for you because [you are drawing an income / you are approaching retirement / you want to maintain your lifestyle and income through retirement] — it means you should not have to sell growth assets through necessity or at depressed prices during a downturn.
alts: A traditional diversified portfolio was discounted as it does not provide the separate Reserves component to smooth volatility at market extremes and provide for your personalised liquidity requirements.
replace: The Reserves structure directly protects your retirement income from sequencing risk; we consider this protection to be in your best interests notwithstanding the higher cost relative to [your current fund / a basic option].

This is aligned to your [risk profile] risk profile and your goal of {goal}.

This supports your goal of {goal} by keeping your strategy on track.

replace: The discipline the managed account provides is, in our view, worth the additional cost over [a self-managed / lower-cost option].
